title: 4.3 Small Group · Group 2
contentObjective: I can estimate the percent of a number using benchmark percents, rounding, and compatible numbers, explain why the method works, and use it on a problem I have not seen before.
languageObjective: I can justify my answer to a skeptic and connect it to a second strategy or representation.

vocabulary.definition: A reasoned answer that is close enough to be useful, found without exact computation.
vocabulary.definitionEs: Una respuesta razonada, lo bastante cercana para ser útil, sin cálculo exacto.
vocabulary.example: 8.6% of 216 is about 10% of 220, which is 22.
vocabulary.cloze: A reasoned answer close enough to be useful is an ___.

examples.text: “About 20 pounds” when the exact answer is 18.576
examples.why: Close enough to plan with, found without exact computation.
That is the exact answer, not an estimate.

vocabulary.definition: A friendly percent — 1%, 10%, 25%, 50%, 75%, 100% — used as a landmark for estimating.
vocabulary.definitionEs: Un porcentaje amigable — 1%, 10%, 25%, 50%, 75%, 100% — que sirve de punto de referencia.
vocabulary.example: 4 GB of 6 GB sits between the 50% and 75% marks.
vocabulary.visual: 1% · 10% · 25% · 50% · 75% · 100% — the landmarks you can find mentally.
vocabulary.cloze: A friendly percent used as a landmark, like 10% or 25%, is a ___ ___.

examples.text: Using 50% because half of an amount is easy
examples.why: You can find half in your head.
To find 25%, divide by 4. You can do that in your head.
37% is hard to find in your head. It is not a benchmark.

vocabulary.definition: Numbers close to the originals that are easy to compute with mentally.
vocabulary.definitionEs: Números cercanos a los originales con los que es fácil calcular mentalmente.
vocabulary.visual: 8.6% of 216 → 10% of 220: both nudged to numbers that divide nicely.
vocabulary.cloze: Numbers close to the originals that are easy to compute with are ___ ___.

examples.why: 200 is close by and 10% of it is instant.
It is easy to compute, but far too far from the original.

vocabulary.definition: Two parallel number lines that pair amounts with their percents at the same positions.
vocabulary.definitionEs: Dos rectas paralelas que emparejan cantidades con sus porcentajes en las mismas posiciones.
vocabulary.example: GB on top, percent on the bottom: 1.5 GB lines up with 25%.
vocabulary.cloze: Two parallel lines pairing amounts with their percents form a ___ ___ ___.

examples.why: Each amount lines up with its percent. 1.5 GB is 25% of 6 GB.

examples.text: One line from 0% to 100% with no amounts
examples.why: There is only one line. No amounts line up with the percents.

vocabulary.definition: The quantity that counts as 100% in a problem — and it can change between questions.
vocabulary.definitionEs: La cantidad que representa el 100% en un problema, y puede cambiar entre preguntas.
vocabulary.example: First the whole is 6 GB; for the photos question the whole becomes the 4 GB used.
vocabulary.visual: “Of the USED storage” makes 4 GB the whole — not the 6 GB total.
vocabulary.cloze: The quantity that counts as 100% in a problem is ___ ___.

examples.text: The 60 students in the class when 18 of them walk
examples.why: It is the amount the percent is measured against.
That is the part; the percent describes it, it is not the whole.

vocabulary.definition: Break a percent into friendly pieces that are easy to find.
vocabulary.definitionEs: Separar un porcentaje en partes fáciles de calcular.
vocabulary.cloze: Breaking 15% into 10% plus 5% is called ___ the percent.

examples.why: The percent is split into easy pieces.
That uses the whole percent at once.

turnAndTalk.question: Margaret's phone has 6 GB total and 4 GB used. On the double number line, 4 GB lands between the 50% mark (3 GB) and the 75% mark (4.5 GB), closer to 4.5. Why does that make 'about 70%' a reasonable estimate instead of an exact one?
turnAndTalk.kernel: 4 GB sits between two benchmark landmarks on the number line, closer to the 75% mark, so a reasonable estimate lands near there without computing the exact fraction.

stems.en: 4 GB is between the ___% mark and the ___% mark, closer to ___%.
stems.es: 4 GB está entre la marca de ___% y la marca de ___%, más cerca de ___%.

turnAndTalk.extend: The Green-Team recycled 216 pounds of material, and 8.6% was metal. Justify why rounding to '10% of 220' gives a reasonable estimate, even though neither number is exact.
extendStems: 8.6% rounds to ___% and 216 rounds to ___ because ___.
Both roundings are reasonable because they are ___ to the original numbers.

turnAndTalk.question: You sorted moves like 'treating 24% as 25%' and 'changing 216 pounds to 200 pounds' into benchmark percent versus compatible numbers. What's the difference between those two strategies?
turnAndTalk.kernel: A benchmark percent replaces the PERCENT with a friendly one (24% → 25%); compatible numbers replace the QUANTITY with a friendly one (216 → 200).

stems.en: Treating 24% as 25% is a benchmark percent because it changes the ___.
stems.es: Tratar 24% como 25% es un porcentaje de referencia porque cambia el ___.

stems.en: Changing 216 to 200 is compatible numbers because it changes the ___.
stems.es: Cambiar 216 a 200 son números compatibles porque cambia la ___.

turnAndTalk.extend: Estimating 8.6% of 216 often uses BOTH strategies at once: 10% of 220. Explain how using both together makes the mental math easier than using just one.
extendStems: Using both, I round the percent to ___ and the number to ___, so the multiplication becomes ___.
Using only one strategy would leave ___ still hard to compute mentally.

turnAndTalk.question: Photos take up 3.5 GB of the 4 GB of USED storage. Why does the whole change from 6 GB to 4 GB for this question, and why would using 6 GB give the wrong percent?
turnAndTalk.kernel: The whole is set by what the question is 'of' — 'of the used storage' makes 4 GB the new 100%, not the phone's full 6 GB capacity.

stems.en: The whole for this question is ___ GB because the question asks 'of the ___.'
stems.es: El todo para esta pregunta es ___ GB porque la pregunta dice 'de ___.'

stems.en: Using 6 GB as the whole would give the wrong answer because ___.
stems.es: Usar 6 GB como el todo daría una respuesta incorrecta porque ___.

turnAndTalk.extend: If instead the question asked 'what percent of the TOTAL storage are photos,' would the answer still be about 87%? Explain what would change.
extendStems: No, because the whole would go back to ___ GB instead of ___ GB.
3.5 out of 6 GB would be about ___%, which is (higher/lower) than 87% because the whole got ___.

turnAndTalk.question: Look back at a problem where you estimated a percent using rounding. What did you round, and which direction did each rounding push your estimate?
turnAndTalk.kernel: Rounding both the percent and the quantity UP (like 8.6% to 10% and 216 to 220) pushes the estimate higher than the exact answer; rounding down pushes it lower.

stems.en: I rounded ___ up/down to ___, which made my estimate ___ than the exact answer.
stems.es: Redondeé ___ hacia arriba/abajo a ___, lo cual hizo mi estimación ___ que la respuesta exacta.

stems.en: I know my estimate is reasonable because ___.
stems.es: Sé que mi estimación es razonable porque ___.

turnAndTalk.extend: A classmate estimated 19% of 412 by rounding to 20% of 400 and got 80. How would you help them check whether 80 is a little high or a little low compared to the exact answer?
extendStems: Since both 19% and 412 rounded ___, the estimate 80 is probably a little ___ than exact.
I would tell them to check by noticing that ___ rounded up and ___ rounded up too.

launch.narrative: This is your challenge small group for Lesson 4.3. You can already get the answer — so in here the answer is the starting point. We ask when the method holds, when it breaks, and how you would convince someone who disagrees.

conceptIntro.heading: Estimate the Percent of a Number
conceptIntro.intro: You can combine benchmark percents to estimate, and you can tell if your estimate is high or low.
conceptIntro.introEs: Puedes combinar porcentajes de referencia para estimar, y puedes saber si tu estimación es alta o baja.
conceptIntro.keyIdea: Benchmark percents can be combined, and the way you round tells you if your estimate is high or low.
conceptIntro.keyIdeaEs: Los porcentajes de referencia se pueden combinar, y la forma en que redondeas te dice si tu estimación es alta o baja.

iDo.title: Example · Combine benchmarks, then judge
iDo.titleEs: Ejemplo · Combina referencias y luego juzga
lines: A school raised $398. About 74% of the money came from a bake sale. Estimate the bake sale money. Is your estimate a little high or a little low?
Round both numbers to friendly numbers: 74% → 75%; $398 → $400
Decide if the estimate is high or low: 75% > 74%; $400 > $398
About $300. The estimate is a little high, because both numbers were rounded up. The exact amount is $294.52.
linesEs: Una escuela recaudó $398. Aproximadamente el 74% del dinero vino de una venta de pasteles. Estima el dinero de la venta de pasteles. ¿Tu estimación es un poco alta o un poco baja?
Redondea los dos números a números amigables: 74% → 75%; $398 → $400
Divide los dos entre 4 para hallar el 25%: 400 ÷ 4 = 100
Multiplica los dos por 3 para hallar el 75%: 100 × 3 = 300
Decide si la estimación es alta o baja: 75% > 74%; $400 > $398
Aproximadamente $300. La estimación es un poco alta, porque los dos números se redondearon hacia arriba. La cantidad exacta es $294.52.

weDo.title: Try it together — then prove it
lines: The Green Team recycled 216 pounds of material. 8.6% of it was metal. Estimate the pounds of metal. Is your estimate high or low?
Round 8.6% and 216 to friendly numbers. (About 10% and about 220.)
Divide 100% and 220 by 10. How many pounds is 10%? (22)
Is 22 pounds more or less than the exact amount? Why? (More. Both numbers were rounded up: 8.6% to 10% and 216 to 220.)
linesEs: El Equipo Verde recicló 216 libras de material. El 8.6% era metal. Estima las libras de metal. ¿Tu estimación es alta o baja?
Redondea 8.6% y 216 a números amigables. (Aproximadamente 10% y aproximadamente 220.)
Divide 100% y 220 entre 10. ¿Cuántas libras son el 10%? (22)
¿22 libras es más o menos que la cantidad exacta? ¿Por qué? (Más. Los dos números se redondearon hacia arriba: 8.6% a 10% y 216 a 220.)

youDo.title: Your turn
lines: A coat costs $61. Today it is 48% off. Estimate the discount in dollars.
One number was rounded up and one was rounded down. Can you tell if $30 is high or low? Explain.
linesEs: Un abrigo cuesta $61. Hoy tiene 48% de descuento. Estima el descuento en dólares.
Un número se redondeó hacia arriba y otro hacia abajo. ¿Puedes saber si $30 es alto o bajo? Explica.

examples.problem: A school raised $398. About 74% of the money came from a bake sale. Estimate the bake sale money. Is your estimate a little high or a little low?

steps.do: Round both numbers to friendly numbers.

steps.why: 75% and $400 are close to the real numbers and easy to use.

steps.doEs: Divide los dos entre 4 para hallar el 25%.

steps.do: Decide if the estimate is high or low.

steps.why: Both numbers were rounded up. So the estimate is a little high.

examples.answer: About $300. The estimate is a little high, because both numbers were rounded up. The exact amount is $294.52.
examples.answerEs: Aproximadamente $300. La estimación es un poco alta, porque los dos números se redondearon hacia arriba. La cantidad exacta es $294.52.

together.title: Try it together — then prove it
together.problem: The Green Team recycled 216 pounds of material. 8.6% of it was metal. Estimate the pounds of metal. Is your estimate high or low?
together.problemEs: El Equipo Verde recicló 216 libras de material. El 8.6% era metal. Estima las libras de metal. ¿Tu estimación es alta o baja?

steps.ask: Divide 100% and 220 by 10. How many pounds is 10%?
steps.askEs: Divide 100% y 220 entre 10. ¿Cuántas libras son el 10%?

steps.ask: Is 22 pounds more or less than the exact amount? Why?
steps.askEs: ¿22 libras es más o menos que la cantidad exacta? ¿Por qué?
steps.answer: More. Both numbers were rounded up: 8.6% to 10% and 216 to 220.
steps.answerEs: Más. Los dos números se redondearon hacia arriba: 8.6% a 10% y 216 a 220.

together.answer: About 22 pounds. It is a little high. The exact amount is 18.576 pounds.
together.answerEs: Aproximadamente 22 libras. Es un poco alta. La cantidad exacta es 18.576 libras.

tryIt.problem: A coat costs $61. Today it is 48% off. Estimate the discount in dollars.
tryIt.problemEs: Un abrigo cuesta $61. Hoy tiene 48% de descuento. Estima el descuento en dólares.
tryIt.hint: 48% is close to 50%. $61 is close to $60. Find half of 60.
tryIt.hintEs: 48% está cerca de 50%. $61 está cerca de $60. Halla la mitad de 60.
tryIt.explain: One number was rounded up and one was rounded down. Can you tell if $30 is high or low? Explain.
tryIt.explainEs: Un número se redondeó hacia arriba y otro hacia abajo. ¿Puedes saber si $30 es alto o bajo? Explica.
tryIt.modelExplanation: Not from the rounding alone. 48% went up to 50%, but $61 went down to $60, so the changes pull in opposite ways. The exact discount is 0.48 × 61 = $29.28, so $30 is a little high.
tryIt.modelExplanationEs: No solo con el redondeo. 48% subió a 50%, pero $61 bajó a $60, así que los cambios van en direcciones opuestas. El descuento exacto es 0.48 × 61 = $29.28, así que $30 es un poco alto.

build.bigIdea: Benchmark percents can be combined, and the way you round tells you if your estimate is high or low.
build.bigIdeaEs: Los porcentajes de referencia se pueden combinar, y la forma en que redondeas te dice si tu estimación es alta o baja.

together.problem: A library has 1,212 books. 77% of them are fiction. Estimate the number of fiction books. Is your estimate high or low?
together.problemEs: Una biblioteca tiene 1,212 libros. El 77% son de ficción. Estima el número de libros de ficción. ¿Tu estimación es alta o baja?

steps.ask: Divide 100% and 1,200 by 4. How many books is 25%?
steps.askEs: Divide 100% y 1,200 entre 4. ¿Cuántos libros son el 25%?

steps.ask: Multiply 25% and 300 by 3. How many books is 75%?
steps.askEs: Multiplica 25% y 300 por 3. ¿Cuántos libros son el 75%?

steps.ask: Both numbers were rounded down. Is 900 high or low?
steps.askEs: Los dos números se redondearon hacia abajo. ¿900 es alto o bajo?
steps.answer: Low. The real numbers are both bigger.
steps.answerEs: Bajo. Los números reales son los dos más grandes.

together.answer: About 900 fiction books. The estimate is a little low, because 0.77 × 1,212 = 933.24.
together.answerEs: Aproximadamente 900 libros de ficción. La estimación es un poco baja, porque 0.77 × 1,212 = 933.24.

together.problem: A meal costs $41.80. You want to leave a 15% tip. Estimate the tip.
together.problemEs: Una comida cuesta $41.80. Quieres dejar una propina del 15%. Estima la propina.

steps.ask: Divide 100% and $40 by 20. How much is 5%?
Multiply 5% and $2 by 3. About how much is the tip?
steps.askEs: Multiplica 5% y $2 por 3. ¿Más o menos cuánto es la propina?

steps.ask: Is $6 a little high or a little low? Why?
steps.askEs: ¿$6 es un poco alto o un poco bajo? ¿Por qué?
steps.answer: A little low. We rounded $41.80 down to $40, and 15% did not change.
steps.answerEs: Un poco bajo. Redondeamos $41.80 hacia abajo a $40, y el 15% no cambió.

together.answer: The tip is about $6. It is a little low, because only the price was rounded, and it went down.
together.answerEs: La propina es aproximadamente $6. Es un poco baja, porque solo se redondeó el precio, y bajó.

onMyOwn.problemEs: Estima el 61% de 497. Combina porcentajes de referencia.
onMyOwn.hint: Round to 60% and 500. Find 10% first, then multiply by 6.
onMyOwn.hintEs: Redondea a 60% y 500. Halla primero el 10%, luego multiplica por 6.

steps.doEs: Redondea a números compatibles.
Divide los dos entre 10 para hallar el 10%.
Multiplica los dos por 6 para hallar el 60%.

onMyOwn.problem: Estimate 11% of 516 with benchmarks. Is your estimate a little high or a little low?
onMyOwn.problemEs: Estima el 11% de 516 con referencias. ¿Tu estimación es un poco alta o un poco baja?
onMyOwn.hint: Round 11% to 10% and 516 to 500. Then think about which way you rounded.
onMyOwn.hintEs: Redondea 11% a 10% y 516 a 500. Luego piensa hacia dónde redondeaste.

steps.doEs: Redondea a números compatibles.

steps.do: Find the scale factor from 100 to 10.
steps.doEs: Halla el factor de escala de 100 a 10.
Divide el entero entre 10 también.

onMyOwn.explain: Is 50 high or low? How do you know?
onMyOwn.explainEs: ¿50 es alto o bajo? ¿Cómo lo sabes?
onMyOwn.modelExplanation: It is a little low. I rounded 11% down to 10% and 516 down to 500. Smaller numbers give a smaller answer. The exact amount is 56.76.
onMyOwn.modelExplanationEs: Es un poco bajo. Redondeé 11% hacia abajo a 10% y 516 hacia abajo a 500. Números más pequeños dan una respuesta más pequeña. La cantidad exacta es 56.76.

onMyOwn.problem: A concert hall has 2,415 seats. On Friday, 49% of the seats were filled. About how many seats were filled?
onMyOwn.problemEs: Una sala de conciertos tiene 2,415 asientos. El viernes se llenó el 49% de los asientos. ¿Aproximadamente cuántos asientos se llenaron?
onMyOwn.hint: 49% is close to a benchmark. Round 2,415 to a number that is easy to halve.
onMyOwn.hintEs: El 49% está cerca de una referencia. Redondea 2,415 a un número fácil de dividir a la mitad.

steps.doEs: Redondea a números compatibles.

steps.do: Find the scale factor from 100 to 50.
steps.doEs: Halla el factor de escala de 100 a 50.
Divide el entero entre 2 también.

onMyOwn.problem: Nia estimates 4.8% of 610. She says 10% of 600 is 60, so the answer is about 60. Find a better estimate.
onMyOwn.problemEs: Nia estima el 4.8% de 610. Dice que el 10% de 600 es 60, así que la respuesta es aproximadamente 60. Halla una mejor estimación.
onMyOwn.hint: Which benchmark is closest to 4.8%? It is half of 10%.
onMyOwn.hintEs: ¿Qué referencia está más cerca de 4.8%? Es la mitad del 10%.

steps.doEs: Redondea a números compatibles.
Divide los dos entre 10 para hallar el 10%.
Divide los dos entre 2 para hallar el 5%.

onMyOwn.modelExplanation: She rounded 4.8% to 10%, but 4.8% is much closer to 5%. 5% is half of 10%, so the estimate is 60 ÷ 2 = 30. Her estimate was about twice too big.
onMyOwn.modelExplanationEs: Ella redondeó 4.8% a 10%, pero 4.8% está mucho más cerca de 5%. El 5% es la mitad del 10%, así que la estimación es 60 ÷ 2 = 30. Su estimación era como el doble de grande.

connect.scenario: Margaret's storage: 6 GB total, 4 GB used, and 3.5 GB of the used space is photos. The rest of the used space is mail, messages, and documents.
connect.promptQuestion: Of the USED storage, approximately what percent are photos — and why does the whole change from 6 GB to 4 GB for this question?
connect.prompt: The whole for this question is ___ . Photos are about ___ % of the used storage, since 3.5 GB sits between the ___ % benchmark and the ___ % benchmark on the number line.

check.stem: For the question 'of the USED storage, what percent are photos,' what is the whole (100%)?
choices: 10 GB, adding the total and used storage together
check.explanation: The whole is set by what the question is ‘of’. This question says ‘of the used storage’. So the 4 GB used becomes the new 100%. The 6 GB total capacity is not the whole here.
check.stemEs: Para la pregunta «del almacenamiento usado, qué porcentaje son fotos», ¿cuál es el entero (100%)?
check.explanationEs: El entero lo fija aquello «de» lo que habla la pregunta. Esta pregunta dice «del almacenamiento usado». Así que los 4 GB usados se vuelven el nuevo 100%. La capacidad total de 6 GB no es el entero aquí.
choicesEs: 10 GB, sumando el almacenamiento total y el usado

check.stem: On a double number line built for a whole of 4 GB, what amount lines up with the 75% mark?
check.explanation: 75% of 4 GB is three-quarters of 4, which is 3 GB. 4.5 GB would be more than the whole itself, and 1 GB is only 25% of 4 GB.
check.stemEs: En una recta numérica doble armada para un entero de 4 GB, ¿qué cantidad se alinea con la marca del 75%?
check.explanationEs: El 75% de 4 GB son tres cuartas partes de 4, que son 3 GB. 4.5 GB sería más que el entero mismo, y 1 GB es solo el 25% de 4 GB.

check.stem: Photos take up 3.5 of the 4 GB of used storage. About what percent of the used storage is photos?
check.explanation: 3.5 GB sits between the 75% mark (3 GB) and the 100% mark (4 GB), much closer to 100% — about 87%. Reading 3.5 as 35% mistakenly treats 10 as the whole instead of 4.
check.stemEs: Las fotos ocupan 3.5 de los 4 GB de almacenamiento usado. ¿Aproximadamente qué porcentaje del almacenamiento usado son fotos?
check.explanationEs: 3.5 GB queda entre la marca del 75% (3 GB) y la del 100% (4 GB), mucho más cerca del 100% — como el 87%. Leer 3.5 como 35% trata por error al 10 como el entero en vez del 4.

connect.modelAnswer: For this question the whole is 4 GB, because we are asked about the used storage — the 6 GB total does not matter now. On a double number line for 4 GB, 75% is 3 GB and 100% is 4 GB. Photos take 3.5 GB, halfway between those marks, so photos are about 87% of the used storage.
connect.promptEs: El entero de esta pregunta es ___ . Las fotos son como el ___ % del almacenamiento usado, ya que 3.5 GB queda entre la referencia del ___ % y la del ___ % en la recta numérica.
connect.scenarioEs: El almacenamiento de Margaret: 6 GB en total, 4 GB usados, y 3.5 GB del espacio usado son fotos. El resto del espacio usado es correo, mensajes y documentos.
connect.promptQuestionEs: Del almacenamiento usado, ¿aproximadamente qué porcentaje son fotos — y por qué el entero cambia de 6 GB a 4 GB en esta pregunta?
connect.modelAnswerEs: Para esta pregunta el entero son 4 GB, porque nos preguntan por el almacenamiento usado — el total de 6 GB no importa ahora. En una recta numérica doble para 4 GB, el 75% son 3 GB y el 100% son 4 GB. Las fotos ocupan 3.5 GB, a la mitad entre esas marcas, así que las fotos son como el 87% del almacenamiento usado.

onLevel.stem: The Green-Team recycled 216 pounds; 8.6% was metal. Using compatible numbers 10% and 200, the estimate is:
choiceFeedback: That is 1% of 200 — the decimal moved one place too far.
That reads 8.6% as 86 pounds.
That subtracts 8 from 216 instead of taking a percent.
hints: Write 10% as a decimal.
One tenth of 200.
onLevel.stemEs: El Equipo Verde recicló 216 libras; 8.6% era metal. Usando los números compatibles 10% y 200, la estimación es:
hintsEs: Escribe 10% como decimal.
Un décimo de 200.

onLevel.stem: Photos use 3.5 GB of the 4 GB of used storage. About what percent of the USED storage is photos?
onLevel.explanation: The whole is 4 GB here. 75% of 4 is 3 GB and 100% is 4 GB; 3.5 sits midway — about 87%.
choiceFeedback: That reads 3.5 GB as 35% — the whole is 4, not 10.
That uses 6 GB as the whole, but the question asks about the USED storage.
3.5 out of 4 is clearly below 100%, but not that close to it.
hints: What is the whole for THIS question?
The whole is 4 GB, not 6.
3.5 of 4 is between the 75% and 100% marks.
onLevel.stemEs: Las fotos usan 3.5 GB de los 4 GB de almacenamiento usado. ¿Aproximadamente qué porcentaje del almacenamiento USADO son las fotos?
onLevel.explanationEs: Aquí el entero es 4 GB. 75% de 4 son 3 GB y 100% son 4 GB; 3.5 queda a la mitad — aproximadamente 87%.
hintsEs: ¿Cuál es el entero para ESTA pregunta?
El entero es 4 GB, no 6.
3.5 de 4 está entre las marcas de 75% y 100%.

onLevel.stem: Why did the whole change between the two storage questions?
choices: The phone gained storage between the questions
The whole never changes in a percent problem
The second question asks about the used storage, so 4 GB becomes 100%
Because photos are more important than mail
onLevel.explanation: Each percent question defines its own whole. 'Of the used storage' makes the 4 GB the new 100%.
choiceFeedback: The phone's capacity never changed — the QUESTION changed.
The whole is set by the question, and this pair of questions sets it differently.
Importance has nothing to do with which quantity is the whole.
hints: Re-read: 'Of the USED storage…'
Which quantity is that question about?
That quantity becomes 100%.
onLevel.stemEs: ¿Por qué cambió el entero entre las dos preguntas del almacenamiento?
onLevel.explanationEs: Cada pregunta de porcentaje define su propio entero. 'Del almacenamiento usado' convierte los 4 GB en el nuevo 100%.
hintsEs: Vuelve a leer: 'Del almacenamiento USADO…'
¿De cuál cantidad trata esa pregunta?
Esa cantidad se convierte en el 100%.
choicesEs: El teléfono ganó almacenamiento entre una pregunta y otra
El entero nunca cambia en un problema de porcentaje
La segunda pregunta trata del almacenamiento usado, así que 4 GB pasa a ser el 100%
Porque las fotos son más importantes que el correo

onLevel.explanation: 24% is about 25%, and 81 is about 80. One quarter of 80 is 20.
choiceFeedback: 2 is about 2.5% of 81 — far below 24%.
8 is about 10% of 81, not 24%.
40 would be about half of 81, but 24% is about a quarter.
hints: Which benchmark is 24% near?
25% is one quarter.
One quarter of 80.
onLevel.stemEs: Estima el 24% de 81 con puntos de referencia.
onLevel.explanationEs: 24% es aproximadamente 25%, y 81 es aproximadamente 80. Una cuarta parte de 80 es 20.
hintsEs: ¿A cuál punto de referencia se acerca el 24%?
25% es una cuarta parte.
Una cuarta parte de 80.

extending.label: Complete the benchmark table for 240.
extending.labelEs: Completa la tabla de puntos de referencia para 240.
hints: 10% and 1% only move the decimal point — no long computation.
25% is half of 50%: once you have 120, halve it again.
hintsEs: 10% y 1% solo mueven el punto decimal: sin cálculos largos.
25% es la mitad de 50%: cuando tengas 120, divídelo a la mitad otra vez.
extending.explanation: The four benchmarks of 240: 10% moves the decimal to 24; 1% moves it again to 2.4; 50% is half, 120; and 25% halves that to 60. Every harder percent in this lesson is built by combining exactly these four.
extending.explanationEs: Los cuatro puntos de referencia de 240: 10% mueve el decimal a 24; 1% lo mueve otra vez a 2.4; 50% es la mitad, 120; y 25% divide eso a la mitad, 60. Cada porcentaje más difícil de esta lección se construye combinando exactamente estos cuatro.

extending.label: Match each percent problem to the benchmark combination that estimates it.
extending.labelEs: Empareja cada problema de porcentaje con la combinación de referencias que lo estima.
hints: Break the percent into benchmark pieces first: 15% = 10% + 5%, and 5% is half of 10%.
Check that the pieces really add to the target percent before trusting the estimate.
hintsEs: Separa el porcentaje en piezas de referencia primero: 15% = 10% + 5%, y 5% es la mitad de 10%.
Verifica que las piezas realmente sumen el porcentaje buscado antes de confiar en la estimación.
extending.explanation: Benchmarks combine like building blocks: 15% is 10% plus its half; 75% is 50% plus 25%; 20% is 10% doubled; 11% is 10% plus 1%. Each combination turns a hard percent into two easy mental moves — the exact strategy behind the Green-Team estimate in this lesson.
extending.explanationEs: Los puntos de referencia se combinan como bloques: 15% es 10% más su mitad; 75% es 50% más 25%; 20% es 10% duplicado; 11% es 10% más 1%. Cada combinación convierte un porcentaje difícil en dos pasos mentales fáciles: la misma estrategia de la estimación del Equipo Verde en esta lección.

extending.stem: Your estimate for 8.6% of 216 was 22 pounds (using 10% of 220). Is the exact answer higher or lower than 22?
choices: Higher, because rounding always shrinks the answer
Lower, because both 10% and 220 rounded UP
extending.explanation: 8.6% went up to 10% and 216 went up to 220, so the estimate overshoots — the exact answer (about 18.6) is lower.
choiceFeedback: Rounding can push an estimate either way; here both pushes were upward.
Exactness is what we gave up when we rounded.
You CAN tell, by looking at which direction each rounding moved.
hints: Which way did each number round?
Both rounded up.
So the estimate is a little high.
extending.stemEs: Tu estimación del 8.6% de 216 fue 22 libras (usando 10% de 220). ¿La respuesta exacta es mayor o menor que 22?
extending.explanationEs: 8.6% subió a 10% y 216 subió a 220, así que la estimación se pasa — la respuesta exacta (aproximadamente 18.6) es menor.
hintsEs: ¿Hacia dónde se redondeó cada número?
Los dos se redondearon hacia arriba.
Así que la estimación queda un poco alta.
choicesEs: Más alto, porque redondear siempre reduce la respuesta
Más bajo, porque tanto 10% como 220 se redondearon HACIA ARRIBA

extending.stem: Estimate 47% of 312. Show which strategy you used — benchmark, rounding, or compatible numbers — and give your estimate.
extending.modelAnswer: 47% is about 50%, and 312 is about 300. Half of 300 is 150, so 47% of 312 is about 150. I used a benchmark (50%) with a compatible number (300).
extending.stemEs: Estima el 47% de 312. Muestra qué estrategia usaste — punto de referencia, redondeo o números compatibles — y da tu estimación.
sentenceStemsEs: El ___% está cerca del punto de referencia ___ .

extending.stem: 1 MB equals 0.001 GB. Mail uses 300 MB. About what percent of Margaret's 6 GB is mail?
extending.explanation: 300 MB is 0.3 GB. 0.3 of 6 is 0.05, which is 5%.
choiceFeedback: 0.5% of 6 GB would be only 0.03 GB.
30% of 6 GB would be 1.8 GB, six times the mail.
That misplaces the decimal — 50% would be 3 GB, ten times the mail.
hints: Convert first: 300 MB = ? GB.
0.3 out of 6 is what fraction?
extending.stemEs: 1 MB equivale a 0.001 GB. El correo usa 300 MB. ¿Aproximadamente qué porcentaje de los 6 GB de Margaret es el correo?
extending.explanationEs: 300 MB son 0.3 GB. 0.3 de 6 es 0.05, que es 5%.
hintsEs: Convierte primero: 300 MB = ? GB.
0.3 de 6 es ¿qué fracción?

extending.stem: Two students estimate 8.6% of 216. Ana uses 10% of 220 = 22. Ben uses 10% of 200 = 20. Whose estimate is closer to the exact answer, 18.576?
choices: Ben's — 20 is 1.4 away; Ana's 22 is 3.4 away
extending.explanation: Exact is 18.576. Ben's 20 misses by about 1.4; Ana's 22 misses by about 3.4. Compatible numbers won this one.
choiceFeedback: 22 − 18.576 = 3.424, which is farther than Ben's 1.424.
The two distances are 1.4 and 3.4 — not equal.
Both are valid estimates; the question is which lands closer.
hints: Find each distance from 18.576.
1.4 versus 3.4.
extending.stemEs: Dos estudiantes estiman el 8.6% de 216. Ana usa 10% de 220 = 22. Ben usa 10% de 200 = 20. ¿Cuál estimación está más cerca de la respuesta exacta, 18.576?
extending.explanationEs: Lo exacto es 18.576. El 20 de Ben falla por unos 1.4; el 22 de Ana falla por unos 3.4. Los números compatibles ganaron esta vez.
hintsEs: Halla la distancia de cada uno a 18.576.
1.4 contra 3.4.
choicesEs: La de Ana — 22 está más cerca de 18.576
La de Ben — 20 está a 1.4 de distancia; el 22 de Ana está a 3.4

extending.stem: For which problem is ESTIMATING clearly the right tool, rather than exact computation?
choices: Deciding if a $58 jacket at 25% off fits your $45 budget
Programming a bank to compute interest on every account
extending.explanation: A quick benchmark — 25% of 60 is 15, so about $43 — answers the budget question; the others need exactness.
choiceFeedback: Bank interest must be computed exactly, to the cent.
Medicine doses can never be 'about right'.
Test scoring has to be exact for every student.
hints: Where is 'close enough' good enough?
Money decisions you make in an aisle are estimates.
The other three carry real risk if inexact.
extending.stemEs: ¿Para cuál problema es ESTIMAR claramente la herramienta correcta, en vez del cálculo exacto?
extending.explanationEs: Un punto de referencia rápido — 25% de 60 es 15, o sea unos $43 — responde la pregunta del presupuesto; los demás casos necesitan exactitud.
hintsEs: ¿Dónde basta con 'lo bastante cerca'?
Las decisiones de dinero que tomas en un pasillo de la tienda son estimaciones.
Las otras tres tienen un riesgo real si no son exactas.
choicesEs: Decidir si una chaqueta de $58 con 25% de descuento cabe en tu presupuesto de $45
Programar un banco para calcular los intereses de cada cuenta
Informar la dosis de un medicamento

revealWordProblem.title: Apply: The Food Drive
revealWordProblem.text:
The organizers of a food drive set a new goal for a second food drive. They hope to collect 140% as many cans as they did last time, when they collected 145 cans.
Question: About how many cans can the organizers expect to collect? Explain your reasoning.
revealWordProblem.sampleAnswer: Estimate with benchmark percents. 145 rounds to 150, and 140% is 100% + 40%. 100% of 150 is 150, and 40% of 150 is 60, so 150 + 60 = 210 cans — about 200. Checking exactly: 1.4 × 145 = 203, which is close to the estimate, so about 200 cans is a reasonable expectation.
